::: {#sol-ce-logit-grad}

By [the log softmax theorem](feedforward-networks.qmd#thm-log-softmax),
$L = \operatorname{LSE}(\vz) - z_y$, where $\operatorname{LSE}$ is [log-sum-exp](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-log-sum-exp).

$$
\begin{aligned}
\derivf{\operatorname{LSE}(\vz)}{z_m}
&= \derivf{}{z_m} \log \sumto{k}{C} \e{z_k}
&& \text{(definition of $\operatorname{LSE}$)} \\
&= \frac{1}{\sumto{k}{C} \e{z_k}} \derivf{}{z_m} \sumto{k}{C} \e{z_k}
&& \text{(chain rule for $\log$)} \\
&= \frac{\e{z_m}}{\sumto{k}{C} \e{z_k}}
&& \text{(only term $k = m$ depends on $z_m$)} \\
&= \operatorname{softmax}(\vz)_m
&& \text{(the [softmax function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/multiclass-logistic-regression.html#def-softmax))}
\end{aligned}
$$

The second term, $z_y$, has derivative 1 with respect to $z_y$ and 0 with respect to every other logit.
So

$$
\derivf{L}{z_m} = \operatorname{softmax}(\vz)_m - \indicf{m = y}.
$$

:::
